blocks.x: The engineering substrate, as deployed in current programs:

items: Bedrock
Managed foundation-model access inside your VPC — no data leaving the estate to get an answer.
Kinesis And Lambda
Server-side streaming for AWS estates — small components, clear owners, costs that show per decision.
S3, Glue And Lake Formation
The AWS lakehouse primitives, wired with column-level permissions from day one.
Ecs And Step Functions
Server-side orchestration on AWS — durable workflows without a scheduler to babysit.
Sagemaker Where Custom Models Earn Their Keep
Custom training only where the math pays back; managed endpoints where it does not.
cost-aware clustering
Workloads land on the cheapest compute that still meets the latency budget.
dbt transformation graph
Tested, documented models with lineage exposure — the transform layer your analysts can actually read.
Unity Catalog governance
A single governance plane over tables, models and notebooks — access your auditors can replay.
Delta / Iceberg tables
Open table formats underneath everything we build, so your data never belongs to a vendor.

blocks.x: Joint delivery on AWS Alliance is designed for handover from the first week — runbooks written as we go, decisions mapped to your owners, nothing that only we can operate.
Artifacts, not anecdotes — at the first-quarter close your team holds:

items: Joint architecture pack
a tenancy-specific architecture pack co-signed by Achala IT Solutions and the vendor platform team
Certified delivery pod
delivery engineers certified on both stacks, so the vendor channel is a colleague, not a ticket queue
Support map
an escalation map exercised in a joint drill, so the first real page is not the first test
